DILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 109 s. 2022 September 30, 2022 ATTY. JULIET CZARINA FURIA Assistant Provincial Legal Officer Province of Agusan del Norte jvfuria@yahoo.com Dear Atty. Furia: This has reference to your e-mail dated September 12, 2022 requesting the Department's legal opinion on whether or not Section 192 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 can be made as basis of your Province in granting incentives on the imposition of real property taxes even if said Section 192 and the topic on Real Property Taxation are discussed in the different parts of the Local Government Code of 1991. Per your representation, your Province is currently in the process of amending your Local Investment and Incentive Code. In reply thereto, we answer in the affirmative. At the outset, may we re-state Section 192 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991: - Local "SECTION 192. Authority to Grant Tax Exemption Privileges. government units may, through ordinances duly approved, grant tax exemptions, incentives or reliefs under such terms and conditions as they may deem necessary." Well-settled is the rule in statutory construction that statutes are to be read as a whole, in context, and, if possible, the court is to give effect to every word of the statute. The court is bound to give consistent, harmonious, and sensible effect to all of the parts of a statute, to the extent possible. It is assumed that the Legislature does not intend to create inconsistency. In the case of Valera vs. Tuasonl, the Supreme Court discussed this rule: "One of the well-established rules of statutory construction enioins that endeavor should be made to harmonize the provisions of a law or two laws so that each shall be effective. In order that one law may operate to repeal another law, the two laws must actually be inconsistent. The former must be so repugnant as to be irreconciliable with the latter act. 1 G.R. No. L-1276, April 30, 1948. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(U.s. vs. Palacios, 33 Phil. , 208.) Merely because a later enactment may relate to the same subject matter as that of an earlier statute is not of itself sufficient to cause an implied repeal of the latter, since the new law may be cumulative or a continuation of the old one. (Statutory Construction, Crawford, p. 634.) The above uoted rovisions can stand to ether. By a fair and reasonable construction, section 73 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, may be said to apply to disqualifications under section 8 of that Act, and section 211 of the Revised Administrative Code to disqualifications or disabilities not embraced in the Code of Civil Procedure." (Emphasis Supplied) A reading of Section 192 and the provisions on real property tax would give us a conclusion that they can be read together. Although the assailed provisions are found in two different books of the LGC, they are embodied in one legislation following the same legislative intent. A logical deduction dictates that the provisions contained therein shall be interpreted in congruence with each other. Section 192 is a general provision as to encompass not only real property tax but also other taxes such as amusement tax. The limitations on the exercise of the authority to grant such tax privileges or exemptions can be seen in Article 282 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code of 1991, viz: Authority to Grant Tax Exemption Privileges or Incentives. "Art. 282. r— (a) While sanggunians may grant tax exemption, tax incentive, or tax relief, such grant shall not apply to regulatory fees which are levied under the police power of LGUs. Tax exemptions shall be conferred through the issuance of a tax exemption certificate, which shall be non-transferable. The sanggunians granting tax exemptions, tax incentives and tax (b) reliefs may be guided by the following: (1) On the grant of tax exemptions or tax reliefs: (i) Tax exemption or tax relief may be granted in cases of natural calamities, civil disturbance, general failure of crops, or adverse economic conditions such as substantial decrease in the prices of agricultural or agri-based products; (ii) The grant of exemption or relief shall be through an ordinance. (iii) Any exemption or relief granted to a type or kind of business shall apply to all business similarly situated; and (iv) Any exemption or relief granted shall take effect only during the next calendar year for a period not exceeding twelve (12) months as may be provided in the ordinance. In the case of shared revenues, the exemption or relief shall only extend to the LGU granting such exemption or relief. (2) On the grant of tax incentives: (i) The tax incentive shall be granted only to new investments in the locality and the ordinance shall prescribe the terms and conditions therefor; page 2 of 3

(ii) (iii) (iv) The grant of the tax incentive shall be for a definite period not exceeding one (I) calendar year; The grant of tax incentives shall be by ordinance passed prior to the first (1st) day of January of any year; and Any tax incentive granted to a type or kind of business shall apply to all businesses similarly situated, The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion issued by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRE ARY: ATTY. AN VICTOR R. LLAMAS Und cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLAJVRLJLLLS-LRALLD/kbm/clp
